the H3 and, in particular, H4 N-terminal tail domains are required to stabilize oligonucleosomes and arrays, and to mediate short- to long-range interactions of the nucleosomal arrays to form higher-order chromatin structures.

the H3 and the H4 N-terminal histone tail domains play a critical role in the folding of nucleosomal arrays into secondary chromatin structure, and that the tail domains mediate short-range and long-range inter-array interactions that are important to higher-order chromatin assembly and organization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the histone H3 and H2A tails are required to stabilize oligonucleosomes and nucleosome fiber, whereas the histone H4 tail is required for fiber stabilization but not oligonucleosome stability.

the H3/H4 tails are important in the formation and stability of higher-order chromatin structures and the H4 tail is a major player in this process, while the H3 tail has a lesser but still important role.

the N-terminal tails are required for nucleosome folding and stabilization, and that the tails of histones H3 and H2A interact in a cooperative fashion to form a nucleosome tail complex that is important for the folding and stabilization of nucleosome arrays.
